scenario.description: A supply chain director must finalize the production and shipment plan for two motor-drive orders when released power modules are insufficient for the orders without quality recovery, with input from process engineering, quality, logistics, and product compliance.

shared_context.S1: The plant must plan production for 240 Model X motor drives and 120 Model Y motor drives in the next production window.
shared_context.S2: Only 450 power modules are currently released for use, while additional modules are physically present in a quality-hold area.
shared_context.S3: Elena makes the binding decision on material allocation, production quantities, and shipment conditions.
shared_context.S4: The daily materials review includes a check with process engineering, quality, logistics, and product compliance before Elena signs the plan; production control policy requires Elena to issue a complete disposition for every scheduled customer order, including a shipment plan or an explicit compliance-gated condition, rather than simply omitting an order.
shared_context.S5: Material-control policy requires the signed allocation to use no more than 450 currently released modules in total and no more than the number of modules explicitly approved for recovery from the quality-hold area; Elena must verify both arithmetic limits before signing.
shared_context.S6: In a signed disposition, a shipment-readiness field means the required verification is committed for completion before the stated shipment, not merely deferred indefinitely; a shipment may proceed only under that completed-before-shipment commitment.

PF1.text: Ravi's engineering bill-of-materials review confirms that each Model X drive requires exactly 2 power modules and each Model Y drive requires exactly 1 power module; he completed the review after the latest engineering change but has not entered the revised quantities in the planning system.

PF2.text: Mara's inspection of the quality-hold area found that exactly 150 of the held modules can be recovered after a 6-hour controlled bake followed by insulation testing; she documented the result in a local inspection worksheet that has not yet been attached to the material record.

PF3.text: Jon's customer confirmations establish that the Model X order may ship as 180 drives on Friday and 60 drives on Monday, while the Model Y customer requires all 120 drives on Friday; he received these confirmations by email but has not updated the shipment board.

PF4.text: Simone's destination review confirms that every Model Y drive must have serialized power-module traceability and a lot-specific compliance certificate before shipment; she completed the review for the export destination but has not added the requirement to the dispatch checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The plan must produce exactly 240 Model X drives and 120 Model Y drives.

The allocation must provide exactly 480 modules for Model X and exactly 120 modules for Model Y, using exactly 450 released modules and 150 recovered modules in total; the released-versus-recovered split between the two models may vary.
Exactly 150 held modules must be recovered.
The recovery process must include a 6-hour controlled bake.
The plan must include insulation testing for the recovered modules.
Model X must ship as exactly 180 drives on Friday and 60 drives on Monday.
All 120 Model Y drives must ship on Friday.
Model Y traceability and certification must be addressed through completed verification or an explicit compliance-verification commitment before shipment.
The plan must address recovery of exactly 150 held modules through the 6-hour bake and insulation testing.
The recovery finding must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C8: decisions['model_y_traceability_verified'] == True or any(c['target'] == 'Simone' and c['type'] == 'compliance_verification' and c['detail'] == 'serialized power-module traceability and lot-specific compliance certificate before shipment' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The exact bill of materials changes the required production quantities to 480 modules for Model X and 120 modules for Model Y, making the full 240-and-120 production plan feasible only when those exact module totals are used.
The inspection result changes the plan from using only 450 released modules to recovering exactly 150 held modules through a 6-hour bake followed by insulation testing.
The customer confirmations change the shipment schedule to 180 Model X drives on Friday, 60 on Monday, and all 120 Model Y drives on Friday.

The destination requirement changes Model Y dispatch from ordinary shipment release to completed or explicitly committed verification of serialized traceability and the lot-specific compliance certificate.
